header:
Date: 2025-11-04 | Start: 09:30 PT | Duration: 75 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (PM), Ethan Zhao (SRE), Maya Lopez (Eng Mgr), Noah Kim (SWE), Priya Raj (Release), Daniel Rivers (CTO), Lina Ortega (Security), Samir Desai (Compliance)
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: okay we're on the record, um, thanks everyone for joining the infra roadmap and launch readiness review. want to do a quick round robin on risks then go into the canary plan. approx 75 minutes so we'll keep it tight.
[00:17] Ethan: hi, uh Ethan here. quick summary from the SRE side — main risk is sustained tail latency under multi-tenant burst, we saw some regressions in the last quantized build. the KV cash warming isn't as effective when sequences are highly variable.
[00:34] Maya: sorry KV cash? do you mean KV cache?
[00:36] Ethan: yes, yes KV cache, sorry the transcript keep doing that. and also the GPU scheduler has a packing issue with 2x short sequences and 1 long, causes head-of-line waits.
[00:50] Noah: uh we observed that too on the 2.7.1 runtime when the compilation picks the slower kernel path for mixed-length micro-batches.
[01:05] Priya: from release POV, my concern is the rollback timeline — if we hit a regression in pricing-sensitive routes we need a documented quick rollback with traffic steering and DNS TTLs. last time we had a 10 minute DNS TTL which hurt us.
[01:22] Aisha: noted. we'll set TTL to 60s for the launch window. next, Lina any security signoffs outstanding?
[01:30] Lina: most are green, but we need KMS key escrow confirmation for the private deploy artifacts and SAML attribute mappings verified for the enterprise SSO flow. Samir is the lead on compliance checklists.
[01:45] Samir: yes we need audit log retention specified — default is 90 days but some customers require 1 year; we need a decision on default plus opt-in longer retention and how it affects storage pricing.
[02:02] Daniel (CTO): for the roadmap chord — I want to make sure the launch doesn't block the 2026 Q1 performance initiatives, i.e., kernel selection improvements. can the launch proceed with an incremental kernel swap later?
[02:18] Ethan: tl;dr: yes, we can ship with the current kernel set and roll the kernel improvements as a live canary, but the canary must have tight MTTI (mean time to investigate) and automated fallback.
[02:33] Aisha: ok let's drill into the canary plan. Priya, you drafted a runbook?
[02:39] Priya: yes I uploaded v0.3 to the shared doc, link in the chat. high level: 1% traffic for first 2 hours, 5% for next 4 hours if stable, then 25% then 50%. automatic fallback when p50 latency + p95 latency exceed thresholds or error rate spikes over 0.5%. we also have manual kill switch.
[03:02] Noah: want to add a step for KV cache pre-warm: we should seed prefixes from our production heatmap to avoid cold-start spikes, otherwise batching won't help.
[03:15] Ethan: agree, plus add a k8s pod warmup sequence and a GPU-allocator prefetch so the allocator isn't stealing time from inference threads.
[03:25] Maya: small ask — include a checklist for quantization toggles per model variant, we had a mismatch last time where the dedicated pool used INT8 and the hosted path used FP16 which caused output drift.
[03:39] Aisha: good point. Noah can you own the tracing instrumentation to detect drift across variants?
[03:45] Noah: yep I'll instrument per-request model-version hash and sample outputs for automatic evaluation. might add noise but useful.
[03:56] Lina: security note — if we seed prefixes we need to ensure no PII ends up in shared cache layers; should we scrub examples or only seed non-customer prefixes?
[04:06] Ethan: we can seed with synthetic prefixes that approximate distribution; the perf team has a generator script but it needs updates to match the current tokenization.
[04:17] Priya: re: monitoring, do we have a combined dashboard? I remember separate dashboards for latency, cost, and token-level billing. For launch we need a single go/no-go dashboard.
[04:29] Maya: I'm working with analytics to bake a dashboard in the console — it will include per-route p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, and model fallback counts. ETA is EOD Friday.
[04:42] Aisha: include a golden metric for the execs — maybe 'cost per 1k tokens at p95 <= $X' and 'successful requests >= 99.8%'. Daniel, sound okay?
[04:53] Daniel: yes that framing is fine. make sure the exec dashboard is distilled.
[05:00] (crosstalk) Ethan: on the point of fallback, we need to test the automatic fallback policy — route from large model to smaller variant and verify stateful sessions degrade gracefully.
[05:12] Noah: we found a session continuity bug when switching model family — conversation context can be lost because of incompatible tokenizer offsets. need to add a converter shim.
[05:25] Maya: am adding the shim task to the engineering backlog — low risk but important for chat-style integrations.
[05:33] Aisha: incident review section — quick postmortem summary from the last incident (2025-10-27). Ethan?
[05:40] Ethan: brief: root cause was overloaded allocator on mixed batch sizes leading to OOM on 2 nodes, autoscaler loop was too slow because of a misconfigured scaleDown grace period. mitigation: improved allocator heuristics and tightened scale metrics. follow-ups: reduce scaleDown grace period, add proactive enqueued request metric.
[06:01] Priya: timeline for mitigations — are those in?
[06:04] Ethan: heuristics merged yesterday but not yet rolled to prod, plan to roll to canary first.
[06:11] Aisha: ok good. discussion: launch timing — are we targeting 2025-11-12?
[06:17] Priya: yes that's the tentative date, need exec sign-off by 2025-11-06.
[06:22] Daniel: scheduling looks fine. one ask: run a competitive smoke test against ModelServeCo's public benchmark to highlight performance delta in the launch blog.
[06:33] Maya: we can, but note their benchmarks are synthetic; we'll run both synthetic and prod-like workloads.
[06:40] (pause) Samir: compliance note — retention decision affects cost and must be documented in the T&Cs; legal will need 48 hour review once we pick the default retention.
[06:50] Aisha: action recaps — I'll summarize after the call. anything else?
[06:55] Ethan: one more thing: circuit breaker thresholds need to be per-customer for dedicated customers vs hosted; otherwise a single noisy tenant could cascade.
[07:07] Noah: we have per-tenant rate-limits but not per-model circuit breaker thresholds, I'll add a schema change to the config service.
[07:16] Aisha: perfect. wrap up — Priya will schedule canary and invite SRE, Maya finalizes playbook, Ethan runs stress tests, Noah instruments tracing, Lina verifies KMS/SAML, Samir and legal finalize retention language. I'll send the go/no-go criteria doc and set the exec review calendar.
[07:38] Priya: noted, I'll create calendar invites after this and link the runbook.
[07:44] Daniel: thanks team, appreciate the thoroughness.
[07:47] Aisha: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
[07:50] (meeting ends)
